Creatures of Sonaria — teardown

SURVIVAL-LOOP · Sonar Studios · placeId 5233782396

A huge creature-survival MMO live since 2020 (2.16B visits, ~36K online). You play as a creature (kaiju/beast): pick a starter, customize its coat and survive by managing stats — Health / Stamina / Food / Water / Oxygen and Age. Eat by diet (Herbivore/Carnivore/Omnivore), sniff the trail to food/water, grow Juvenile → Teen → Adult (new abilities and stats), explore regions and realms (Aquatic/Hardcore/Trade), fight players and co-op bosses (Mawfin/Xorrogon for a title), join packs and trade. On top — a giant collection: hundreds of species via dozens of gachas (Shooms, Tikits, Time Points, event Pearls, Robux), with tiers Tiny(1)→Huge(5) and mutations. This teardown follows the 111-frame recording (a systems tour) cross-checked with the wiki; focus: how a creature-survival sandbox fused with a gacha collection and held an audience across years of seasonal events.

01Classification — game atoms

What the game is at the mechanics level. The core is a SURVIVAL-LOOP (survive as a creature by stats and grow), but on top sits a huge RNG collector (hundreds of species via gachas). It is a survival sandbox with a gacha meta-progression.

Verb
Forage — find and consume food/water (by sniffing the trail) to survive and grow; the repeated input is sniff → eat/drink, plus movement and combat
Theme
'Survive Kaiju Animals': pick a creature → survive by stats (food/water/oxygen/health/stamina) and grow Juvenile→Adult → explore regions/realms, fight or coexist with players → collect hundreds of species via gachas
Core systems
Creature survival (stats + diet + sniff) · growth (age stages) · gacha collection (dozens of gachas, hundreds of species) · combat (PvP + world bosses) · regions/realms · missions · packs/trade · nests/mutations
Economy
Shooms (main: 5 per 2 min + missions → gachas, convert to Tikits) · Tikits (tokens + Mystery/Royalty/Celestial gachas) · Time Points · Pearls (event, wiped) · Robux (starter creature, currency packs, species, bundles, mutations)
Mask
The storefront/name says 'survive the kaiju'; observation confirms the survival but refines it: the long hook and monetization are the creature collection (gachas, tiers, mutations), and survival/growth is what you DO with the creatures you collect
Archetype
SURVIVAL-LOOP — gathering (food/water), maintenance (stats) and risk management (predators/PvP/disasters) extend the creature's life and grow it; on top, an RNG collector of hundreds of species
Progression
Completion by species collection (the Achievement gacha requires 100 species; realms 25+) plus a power-ladder by growth (Juvenile→Adult→Elder, full stats/abilities). Creature tiers Tiny(1)→Huge(5) are a rarity axis
[SURVIVAL-LOOP: forage→survive→grow→collect] + entity-hazards + container-gacha + rng-roll + inventory-equipment + location-ladder + quests + social-multipliers + combat | {creature-survival-mmo · evergreen · shared} × completion-ladder — a creature-survival sandbox + a species-collector gacha; dozens of gachas, tiers 1–5, realms, co-op world bosses and years of seasonal events $ wall:collection-and-growth-grind→offer:currency-and-species ! rarity-ceremony

A 'genre-veteran leader' profile: 6+ years of live-service, 2.16B visits, a high rating. It is a creature-survival benchmark on Roblox (the 'play as a dinosaur/beast' genre), built around two engines at once: a survival sandbox (moment-to-moment play) and a gacha collection (the long meta and monetization). Below is how both halves are built and interlocked.

03FTUE — pick a creature and tutorial

Onboarding is two-phase: first pick a starter creature (with traits) and customize its coat, then an in-world tutorial teaches the survival core — sniff, drink, eat.

The FTUE is 'build a character, then survive'. First the player picks a creature (with readable traits: type, diet, abilities) and paints it — which sets attachment and a collection tone up front. Then a short in-world tutorial teaches three base survival verbs: Sniff (find by trail), Drink (water), Eat (food by diet). The key trick is sniff as navigation: instead of quest arrows the player 'sniffs out' the goal, which suits a beast and makes the world feel alive. A starter badge and first Getting-Started tasks give direction immediately.

04The survival loop: stats & sniff

The moment-to-moment core: five draining stats (Health/Stamina/Food/Water/Oxygen) tick down, and you maintain them with food/water/rest while avoiding predators, PvP and disasters.

The survival loop is 'maintain your stats while you grow and explore'. Five bars drain: Food and Water (the main ones — always ticking; refilled by diet and at water), Health and Stamina (combat/running), Oxygen (underwater — critical in the aquatic realm). Plus Age rises over time and feeding. Sniff finds resources (a trail), and Roll in mud hides your scent from predators/PvP. Danger is not only hunger: other players (PvP), NPC predators, disasters (weather) and world bosses. It is a classic survival loop, but in a creature's body and in a shared MMO world where allies (packs) and threats are always nearby.

05Growth: Juvenile → Adult → Elder

The main power axis: a creature is born a juvenile with reduced stats and grows by age, unlocking full stats, abilities and combat potential. Growth is the reward for surviving.

StageAgeWhat it gives
Juvenilestartreduced stats, fast stamina drain, low damage
Teenage 33an intermediate rise in stats/abilities
Adultage 66full stats, abilities and combat potential
Elder → Venerateage 100+optional late stages (prestige)

Growth is a power-ladder within a single life: a creature is born a weak juvenile and ages up by eating diet-appropriate food. Adulthood (Teen at 33, Adult at 66) unlocks full stats, abilities and combat — so survival is rewarded with power, not just a day count. Each species has its own sheet (Health/Damage/Stamina/Speed, passives and active abilities, growth time), so 'which creature to grow' is a build decision. Realms can speed growth (Hardcore ×2). Age 100 opens prestige stages (Elder/Venerate). So growth stitches survival to collection: collect a species → grow it → gain its power.

06The world: regions, weather, disasters

The open MMO world is split into dozens of biome regions with their own weather and hazards. Regions are both a place to survive and the axis of missions/rewards.

The world is a shared open MMO of dozens of regions (Swamp Hollow, Jungle, Desert, Mesa, Mountains, Coral Reef, Tundra, Volcano Island, Kelp Forest, Redwoods, Seaweed Depths…). On top come weather/eras (Fall, Fog, Famine, Winter, Sakura, Clear Skies) and disasters (which can even be summoned with tokens — Blizzard/Hurricane/Volcano/Earthquake/Blood Moon summon). A region sets diet/resources, and underwater (the aquatic realm) adds Oxygen as a separate stat. For the player, regions are both a survival stage and a progress axis: each has its own missions and rewards (chapter 07), which is why 'visit 3 regions' is one of the first goals.

07Missions — the goal engine

A huge goal system in 6 tabs: Creatures, Gachas, Regions, Event, Timed, Sub-Species. Missions hand out species, gacha tokens and Shooms — that is, they feed the collection.

Missions are the goal engine and a bridge to the collection. Six axes: Creatures (unlock exclusive species), Gachas (earn tokens for spins), Regions (per-biome tasks — which also teach mechanics: attack/heal, sniff, hide scent, travel), Event (event ones), Timed (daily/weekly/monthly + pack missions — a return hook) and Sub-Species (species variants for Shooms). The point — all survival is quantified into tasks, and the rewards (species, tokens, Shooms) feed the gacha collection directly. That is what turns 'just walking around as a beast' into an endless checklist.

08Gachas & the creature collection

The long meta and the main display: dozens of gachas roll hundreds of species by tier and rarity. Cheap ones for Shooms/Tikits, top legendaries and artifacts for huge sums. This is the dopamine core.

Gachas are the heart of the meta and monetization. There are dozens (by diet, Mystery, Featured, Artifact, Royalty/Celestial, Achievement, Bugs/Plants/Hybrids, event gachas), and together they roll hundreds of species with tiers Tiny(1) → Huge(5) and rarities. The economy is a ladder: base species are cheap (65 Shooms, 4% each), top legendaries 15,500, and Artifact runs into the hundreds of thousands to a million Shooms with stacking discounts from secret artifacts. Key hooks: the Achievement gacha is gated behind '100 species' (a collector goal), Auto Skip removes the friction of bulk spins, and the in-world reveal loot box is spectacle. The collection is both a goal ('catch them all') and the main money flow (currencies for gachas).

09Nests, mutations & realms

Depth for veterans: breed creatures in nests, catch mutation variants, and switch realms (Aquatic/Hardcore/Trade) with exclusive bonuses and mutations.

The late-game depth is nests, mutations and realms. Nests let you 'breed' creatures, and offspring/growth can roll a mutation — a rare species variant (via Robux, event items like Clownfish 6%, or the Trade Realm). Realms are separate mode-worlds with their own rules: Aquatic (deep-sea hazards + a MARINE mutation), Hardcore (×2 growth, +20% mutation chance, +25% mission rewards, a GILDED mutation, a Shadow Shrine — gated at '25+ species'), Trade (a player-to-player economy: stalls, auctions on rare-creature slots, server-wide drop parties). This is endgame content: it gives veterans new goals (mutations, trading, hardcore) on top of base survival and holds those who have 'collected everything'.

10Packs, social & trade

This is an MMO: live players are always around. Packs (co-op), a shared chat, invites, and the Trade Realm adds a full player-to-player economy.

The social layer is a full MMO layer, not decoration. Packs are co-op cells: invites right in the world, a shared leader, pack missions (including monthly ones) and co-op takedowns of world bosses for a title. A shared chat and the presence of dozens of players make a living world where you can coexist or fight (PvP). And the Trade Realm adds a player economy: trade stalls (your own shop), auctions on rare-creature slots, and server-wide drop parties. For a survival game this is a strong retention multiplier: the collection becomes social capital (show it, sell it, trade it), and packs give a reason to return with friends.

11Economy & currencies

A layered economy built for collection: Shooms (base, earned by play), Tikits (for premium gachas and tokens), Time Points, event Pearls and Robux. Clear roles.

CurrencyHow to getWhere to spend
Shooms (main)5 per 2 min (~150/hr) + region missions; convert to/from Tikitsgachas, Rotation/Trial shops, sub-species
Tikitsconvert from Shooms or Robux packstokens + Mystery(1)/Royalty(10)/Celestial(20) gachas
Time Pointsover time in gamethe Time Points Shop (species)
Pearls (event)event missions/minigames/Robux; wiped after the eventthe event shop (species/mutations/bundles)
Robux ⬡purchasestarter creature, currency packs, species, bundles, mutations, tokens

The economy is layered but with clear roles, all tuned for the collection. Shooms are the base 'by play' currency (they drip with time + missions), spent to roll most gachas; they can also be converted to Tikits — a premium currency for the Mystery/Royalty/Celestial gachas and tokens. Time Points are a separate species shop. Pearls are event-only and wiped after the season (creating a 'spend it now' urgency). Robux is the bypass: direct purchase of currencies, species, bundles, mutations. The balancing trick: the base loop is free (Shooms over time), but top rarities (Featured/Artifact/mutations) cost tens to hundreds of thousands — which is where Robux saves months of grind.

12Monetization

Entirely on currencies/bundles/species for Robux (not gamepasses). It sells the starter creature, currency packs, direct species, event bundles, tokens (growth/revive/weather) and mutations.

SKUPrice (Robux)What it gives
Starter creature (Saukuryn)⬡39a solid starter creature up front
Currency: Shooms / Pearls / Tikits⬡ varies (+15% Extra)premium/base currency for gachas
Species in the Shop⬡89 … 1,679direct purchase of a specific creature
Bundles: Kelvaris/Logavian / Battle / Predator / Kriffin⬡999 / 999 / 715 / 299 / 225species+currency sets (some event-exclusive)
Tokens⬡ variesGrowth/Revive/Glimmer + weather summons
Palettes / Plushies⬡ variescoat cosmetics / collectible plushies

Monetization is a currency-and-content shop, no gamepasses, entirely via Robux purchases. The levers: starter (a creature for 39⬡ — the 'first dollar'), grind bypass (Shooms/Tikits packs speed gachas; Growth/Revive tokens = growth and a second chance), direct species (89–1679⬡ for a specific creature, skipping RNG), event exclusives (999⬡ bundles on timers — FOMO) and mutations (the rarest — via Robux/Trade). A neat detail — weather summon tokens (call a volcano/storm): they sell not power but an event/chaos for the server. An honest signal — bundles literally say 'all earnable through gameplay', which lowers the pay-to-win feel and holds the 92% rating.

13HUD & menus

The game is huge and the UI reflects it: a quiet game HUD (stats/weather/minimap) + a dense menu hub with dozens of screens (49 flagged). Below — the key ones.

The interface splits the load for the game's scale. In-world the HUD is targeted: a stat bar, weather/region on top, a minimap, a radial action menu (Sniff/Roll/Vocal Calls/Abilities) and active tasks — so survival reads clearly without clutter. Out of the world is a dense menu hub (the main menu with creature slots + Missions, Shop, Creature Shop, Inventory, Social, Realms, Index, Settings). Worth highlighting is the Help Index — a built-in glossary over dozens of terms (ailments, multipliers, abilities): for a game this deep it is the right move — teach via a reference, not a flood of tutorial modals. 49 flagged menu screens are the price of the system depth.

14Retention: events, logins, bosses

A veteran's retention stack: daily logins and missions, an endless gacha collection, co-op world bosses for titles and — above all — a seasonal event every month for six years.

Retention is a strong stack. Short hooks: Daily Points and daily/weekly missions, a Login Shop with a streak, a Loyalty Bonus for joining the group. Medium: the gacha collection (there is always a 'next species'), creature growth, region missions. Long: realms/mutations, the Achievement gacha (100 species), the Trade economy. Live social events: world bosses (Pale Mawfin, Xorrogon in the aquatic realm) — the server co-ops for an exclusive title. And the main pillar — a seasonal event every month (Summer Paradise, Halloween, Winter, Easter…): new species, a Pearls shop, mutations, badges. It is this event machine that has held the audience for six years — visible directly in the badge funnel below.

The funnel reads differently from other games: almost all 44 badges are seasonal events (Land Sea Sky, Halloween, Winter, Easter, Valentines, Summer Paradise, Harvest, Disaster, Fireworks…) across 2020–2026. This is not 'how many reached level N' but a map of return over time by event. Recent 2025–2026 events take 40–77% of the top — that is, the game doesn't lose its audience but holds it in waves: every month a new event returns millions. Old badges (2020–2022) are hundreds of thousands (an earlier, smaller base). The teardown takeaway: for this leader the retention engine is not progression but the event calendar; it is the regular seasonal content, not difficulty, that keeps the live-service alive for six years.

16Sound, VFX and ceremonies

The juice is two-sided: the tactility of survival (eating/sniffing/creature growth) and gacha ceremonies (a rarity loot-box reveal). Below — from the captured moment and observations.

Survival: food, growth, the elements

The survival sound is soft and organic (a moderate transient): the chomp of food, the splash of water, the growls/vocalizations of the creature (there are 4 Vocal Calls — broadcast/friendly/aggressive/chatter). A separate visual layer is bioluminescence and coat (the editor customization), weather/disasters (snow, fog, a volcano — even summoned with tokens) and the growth ceremony 'You grew to adult!'. It makes the world feel alive and 'beastly'.

The gacha reveal: a rarity ceremony

InteractionVisual (VFX)Sound / characterPurpose
Eating/drinkingstats refill, particleschomp / splashthe tactility of survival
Growth (age up)'You grew to adult!' + a model swapa ceremony stingera power milestone
Vocalizationsa creature pose/animation4 Vocal Calls (call/friendly/aggressive)social comms in an MMO
Weather/disastersnow/fog/volcano, an era swapan elemental ambiencerisk + spectacle (summon tokens)
Gacha reveala loot box unfolds, a tier framea reel → reveal stingercollection dopamine

What to take: in a 'survival + collection' hybrid the sound/VFX work on two fronts. Survival — organic and tactile (food/water/vocalizations + the growth ceremony), so the beast's life feels real. Collection — a full gacha ceremony (loot box → reveal → rarity frame), the main repeatable dopamine. Plus customization (coat/bio-light) gives a visual attachment to 'your' creature. Split them: the survival routine is warm and quiet, a rare-species reveal is bright and loud.

19What to take into your project

Concrete decisions from a veteran leader (2.16B visits, 6 years of live-service), portable into your own survival or collection project.

1

Play AS the collectible

You don't collect pets from the outside — you PLAY each creature (survive, grow, fight). Collection and gameplay are the same thing, so 'catch them all' = 'try every play style'.

2

Sniff as navigation instead of quest arrows

Sniff → trail → goal suits a beast better than UI arrows and makes the world alive. Diegetic navigation strengthens the survival roleplay.

3

Growth as a power-ladder within one life

Juvenile→Adult unlocks stats and abilities for surviving. Progress feels present every session even without new creatures: grow the one you have.

4

A layered currency built for collection

Shooms (by play) → base gachas; convert to Tikits → premium gachas; Time Points; event Pearls (wiped = urgency). The base loop is free, top rarities are a paid bypass.

5

A gacha ladder by rarity

From 65 Shooms (4% each) to Artifact 200k–1M with compound discounts and an Achievement gacha requiring 100 species. A cheap entry + an expensive tail hold both newcomers and collectors.

6

Realms as endgame modes

Aquatic/Hardcore/Trade add new rules (×2 growth, mutations, an economy) over the base. Not 'another map' but other ways to play — they retain those who've collected everything.

7

MMO social: packs + trade + co-op bosses

The collection becomes social capital (show/sell/auction it), packs give a reason to return with friends, and world bosses for a title unite the server live.

8

Retention engine = the event calendar, not difficulty

44 badges are almost all seasonal (6 years of monthly events). Regular themed content (species, a shop, mutations, badges) returns millions in waves — that is what keeps the live-service alive.

9

A built-in glossary instead of a wall of tutorials

The Help Index explains dozens of terms (ailments, multipliers, abilities) on demand. For a deep game a reference is cleaner and more honest than a flood of tutorial modals.
